title: Welcome
text:
Hi there, I’m Achilleas! 👋
Welcome to my personal corner of the web, where I delve into the fascinating world of data science.
I’m a data analyst at the UK’s leading provider of public sector early payment programmes and market intelligence. I hold an MSc in Data Analytics and am a GradStat member of the Royal Statistical Society, actively pursuing Chartered status. My weekdays revolve around transforming data into actionable insights. When I’m not behind my desk, you’ll most likely find me behind my piano or in a movie theater.
This blog is where I share my journey as I:

Build my data science portfolio with projects that showcase my skills and expertise.
Create a series of educational articles designed to make data science concepts accessible and practical.
Explore real-world applications of advanced statistical modeling in an attempt to shed light on complex problems.

Whether you’re a fellow professional, a data enthusiast, or just curious about the field, I hope you’ll find value in the content I share.
Let’s connect and continue the conversation!

title: Designing and Maintaining an Accessible Website
text:
Why Accessibility Matters
Accessibility in web design ensures that everyone, including individuals with disabilities, can access and navigate your website. As data scientists, we often present insights, visualizations, and interactive elements, making accessibility even more critical.


Key Principles of Accessible Design

Provide Text Alternatives
Use descriptive alt text for images and ensure screen readers can interpret visual content.
Ensure Keyboard Navigation
Users should be able to navigate your site using only a keyboard (e.g., via tabbing through elements).
Use Sufficient Color Contrast
Maintain a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text to enhance readability for users with visual impairments.
Make Interactive Elements Perceivable
Buttons, links, and form elements should be distinguishable and have clear focus indicators.
Structure Content with Semantic HTML
Use proper HTML elements like <h1>, <h2>, <p>, and <nav> to define content hierarchy.



Maintaining Accessibility Over Time

Test Regularly using tools like WAVE or the browser’s built-in accessibility inspector.
Monitor Contrast and Readability when updating colors, fonts, or layouts.
Check ARIA Attributes to ensure dynamic content remains accessible.
Gather User Feedback from people who rely on assistive technologies.

By incorporating accessibility into your workflow, you create a more inclusive web experience, making your content and insights accessible to all users.
